spaces.name: Bookcase
spaces.benefit: Removing a bookcase does not destroy any of the books stored.

spaces.name: Curtains
spaces.benefit: If another room is placed behind a pair of curtain hotspots such that it blocks the windows, the windows and curtains will be replaced with a wall decoration depending on the type of curtains.

spaces.name: Fireplace
spaces.benefit: Goblin decorations can be used on the fireplace to make a decorated marble fireplace. To light a fire in the fireplace, logs are needed in the inventory.

spaces.name: Rug
spaces.benefit: If the furniture is removed, player will receive their Raging echoes rug back, allowing them to move it to a different room or sell it to another player.

spaces.name: Big Tree / Tree
spaces.benefit: *Note: None of these trees may be chopped down for wood. They are purely decorative. *Note: The level boost from a cup of tea will work, but the crystal saw's boost will NOT work.

spaces.name: Centrepiece
spaces.benefit: It is, as the name suggests, used as an entrance to a player's dungeon. It can only be used to access the dungeon if the player has a stairway conjunction built below the garden.

spaces.name: Tip jar
spaces.benefit: Guests in a player's house may use the tip jar to gift coins and platinum tokens to the house owner.

spaces.name: Barrel
spaces.benefit: Calquat kegs of chef's delight or chef's delight (m) may NOT be substituted for beer glasses during the construction process.

spaces.name: Cat basket
spaces.benefit: Cats, kittens, pet rocks , or Humphrey Dumphrey belonging to anyone can rest on the blanket.

spaces.name: Larder
spaces.benefit: Players can withdraw an unlimited amount of tea leaves, milk, eggs, flour, potatoes, garlic, onions, and cheese from the larder.

spaces.name: Shelf
spaces.benefit: Shelves of all levels provide cups of tea that provide Construction boosts depending on the type.

spaces.name: Sink
spaces.benefit: Players can, using a bucket or other such item, receive water from the sink.

spaces.name: Spice rack
spaces.benefit: Players can use the spice rack to store up to 2,147,483,647 doses of brown, orange, red, and yellow spices.

spaces.name: Stove
spaces.benefit: Players can prepare food on the range using the Cooking skill. This range acts as a normal range, and all food can be cooked on it.

spaces.name: Bell-pull
spaces.benefit: Ringing a bell-pull in your dining room instantly summons your servant, making it very useful.

spaces.name: Curtains
spaces.benefit: If another room is placed behind a pair of curtain hotspots such that it blocks the windows, the windows and curtains will be replaced with a wall decoration depending on the type of curtains.

spaces.name: Decoration
spaces.benefit: Excluding the greenman carving, you must speak to Sir Renitee in White Knights' Castle to obtain a family crest before you can build a decoration.

spaces.name: Fireplace
spaces.benefit: You can only use regular logs to light the fireplace, giving some Firemaking experience.

spaces.name: Seating
spaces.benefit: Benches are used to sit on. They have little practical use but add to the 'dining room' concept.

spaces.name: Clockmaking
spaces.benefit: Players gain Crafting experience for making the items on the table rather than Construction experience.

spaces.name: Heraldry stands
spaces.benefit: The player can make wieldable banners in their family crest colours on the easel, as well as colour steel kiteshields, adamant kiteshields, rune kiteshields, steel full helms, adamant full helms, a…

spaces.name: Repair benches
spaces.benefit: This piece of furniture is useful in its ability to repair armours such as Barrows equipment.

spaces.name: Tool stores
spaces.benefit: Players can withdraw unlimited amounts of rakes, spades, gardening trowels, seed dibbers, watering cans, and secateurs.

spaces.name: Workbenches
spaces.benefit: The player can make all flatpack furniture. As with all workbenches, the player cannot drop items while sitting.

spaces.name: Corner
spaces.benefit: There is currently no purpose for this clock, apart from aesthetics. When the player reads the clock some of the possible things it can say include: "It's twenty to Rune.", "It's a quarter past Run…

spaces.name: Curtains
spaces.benefit: If another room is placed behind a pair of curtain hotspots such that it blocks the windows, the windows and curtains will be replaced with a wall decoration depending on the type of curtains.

spaces.name: Dresser
spaces.benefit: The dressers and oak shaving stand allow the player to access the hairstyles makeover interface.

spaces.name: Fireplace
spaces.benefit: Goblin decorations can be used on the fireplace to make a decorated marble fireplace. To light a fire in the fireplace, logs are needed in the inventory.

spaces.name: Rug
spaces.benefit: If the furniture is removed, player will receive their Raging echoes rug back, allowing them to move it to a different room or sell it to another player.

spaces.name: Wardrobe
spaces.benefit: The wardrobe allows the player to change their basic clothing and shoes. Higher grades offer more options to choose from.

spaces.name: Armour (Castle Wars)
spaces.benefit: Removing the armour stand will return the armour pieces used to build it.

spaces.name: Armour (Smithing)
spaces.benefit: Trimmed armour cannot be used. Removing the armour stand will return the armour pieces used to build it.

spaces.name: Head trophy
spaces.benefit: In addition to basic and superior trophies, it can also display superlative trophies, which include the King Black Dragon and Kalphite Queen.

spaces.name: Fishing trophy
spaces.benefit: Big fish that have been stuffed by the taxidermist can be added to displays whilst in building mode.

spaces.name: Rugs/Stairs
spaces.benefit: A staircase added to a skill hall on the ground floor will prompt the player to build it "Up" or "Down".

spaces.name: Banner stand
spaces.benefit: The player can use the following items on the stand to display it: * * * * * *

spaces.name: Rug
spaces.benefit: If the furniture is removed, player will receive their Raging echoes rug back, allowing them to move it to a different room or sell it to another player.

spaces.name: Outfit stand
spaces.benefit: The player can use any tier of the relic hunter outfits on the stand to display them: * * * * * * Note that tier 3 sets also require the set's matching cane in order to be displayed.

spaces.name: Pedestal (x1)
spaces.benefit: The player can use trophies from leagues they've participated in on the ornate pedestal to display them.

spaces.name: Accomplishment scroll
spaces.benefit: Players can right-click the scroll to view the following: * League-statistics - shows the house owner's general league statistics as well as the league points and trophy earned for each league.

spaces.name: Trophy case
spaces.benefit: The player can use the trophy case to store their trophies from leagues they've participated in.

spaces.name: Elemental balance
spaces.benefit: Players are to use the elemental spells (air, earth, fire and water) to balance the colour of the orb white.

spaces.name: Game
spaces.benefit: The game is played just like Hangman in the real world - guess a letter in the word. If it's in the word, all the spots that match that letter fill in.

spaces.name: Prize chest
spaces.benefit: The player that wins a game can draw prizes from the chest. It can hold up to coins.

spaces.name: Ranging game
spaces.benefit: The Dartboard and Archery Target require the players to bring their own ranged equipment.

spaces.name: Stone
spaces.benefit: Two players have separate combat stones, first one to break the stone is the winner, pieces of this stone may come off and deal damage to the player.

spaces.name: Combat dummy
spaces.benefit: Compared to the undead combat dummy, the ornate undead combat dummy has the advantage of acting as a revenant as well, allowing use of an amulet of avarice over the salve amulet, which provides a +…

spaces.name: Combat ring
spaces.benefit: Using a pugel stick from an extra weapons rack, a player must climb onto the balance beam and use the pugel stick to try and knock the opponent down.

spaces.name: Storage
spaces.benefit: The rack includes boxing gloves, a wooden sword & shield, and a pugel stick. It should be noted that a player cannot wield the pugel stick nor may the player use it in any of the fighting rings oth…

spaces.name: Bookcase
spaces.benefit: Removing a bookcase does not destroy any of the books stored.

spaces.name: Guild trophy
spaces.benefit: An amulet of glory (t) cannot be put as a trophy. A wall-mounted amulet of glory can be used an unlimited number of times without the need to recharge.

spaces.name: Landscape
spaces.benefit: Landscapes are purchased from Sir Renitee who resides on the of Falador Castle for . They require the completion of certain quests to be purchased.

spaces.name: Map
spaces.benefit: Maps are purchased from Sir Renitee who resides on the of Falador Castle for .

spaces.name: Portrait
spaces.benefit: Portraits are purchased from Sir Renitee who resides on the of Falador Castle for . They require the completion of certain quests to be purchased.

spaces.name: Rugs/Stairs
spaces.benefit: A staircase added to a Quest Hall on the ground floor will prompt the player to build it "Up" or "Down".

spaces.name: Sword
spaces.benefit: The swords below are quest rewards and are recovered if the decoration is removed.

spaces.name: Arena
spaces.benefit: The arena serves as a way to have your pets "let off steam" by fighting each other. To use, simply use the desired pets on the arena.

spaces.name: Habitat
spaces.benefit: This space is only available in the outdoor version of the menagerie. These also require a hammer, saw, and watering can.

spaces.name: Pet feeder
spaces.benefit: The pet feeder will automatically care for a kitten following the player if it gets hungry or lonely while the player is in the house.

spaces.name: Pet house
spaces.benefit: Pet houses can store unique pets and up to 12 extras (pet rocks, pet fish, cats, hellcats, toy cats, broavs, eggs, spooky chairs, the mayor of Catherby, and Archibald).

spaces.name: Pet list
spaces.benefit: The pet list will indicate which pets the player owns.

spaces.name: Scratching post
spaces.benefit: The scratching post can be used for your cats to play around. Additionally, some pets possess special dialogue when they attempt to interact with it.

spaces.name: Bookcase
spaces.benefit: Removing a bookcase does not destroy any of the books stored.

spaces.name: Crystal ball
spaces.benefit: Used to change the element of non-combination elemental staves.

spaces.name: Lectern
spaces.benefit: The marble lectern combines the utility of both the mahogany eagle lectern and mahogany demon lectern, allowing players to create all of the standard magic tablets in one lectern.

spaces.name: Telescope
spaces.benefit: A telescope can be used to help players locate a Shooting star.

spaces.name: Armour case
spaces.benefit: Armour cases can be used to store certain armours. A full list of items that can be stored in an armour case can be found at the armour case space article.

spaces.name: Cape rack
spaces.benefit: Cape racks can be used to hang various capes, including Capes of Accomplishment. A list of the capes that can be stored is available at the cape rack space article.

spaces.name: Fancy dress box
spaces.benefit: Fancy dress boxes are used to store various cosmetic outfits from certain random events. Random event sets are obtained by completing the random events several times.

spaces.name: Magic wardrobe
spaces.benefit: Magic wardrobes can be used to store certain magic armours. A list of the magic armours that can be stored is available at the magic wardrobe space article.

spaces.name: Toy box
spaces.benefit: Toy boxes are used to store Holiday rewards. These are usually obtained during festivities such as Christmas, Easter and Halloween.

spaces.name: Treasure chest
spaces.benefit: Treasure chests are used to store Treasure Trails rewards, either bought or discovered by players themselves.

spaces.name: Altar
spaces.benefit: Altars can be used to recharge Prayer points and sacrifice bones for greater Prayer experience than burying them.

spaces.name: Lamps
spaces.benefit: Torches and candlesticks are purely cosmetic, offering no prayer bonus when lit. However, incense burners can be lit to provide an extra 50% experience bonus each to the Prayer experience granted b…

spaces.name: Icons
spaces.benefit: The chapel aligns to either Guthix, Saradomin, Zamorak, or Bob depending on the icon chosen.

spaces.name: Musical
spaces.benefit: The organ can be interacted with using the 'Play' option, but, unlike the windchimes and the bells, the sound can only be heard with music option on.

spaces.name: Statues
spaces.benefit: Building one statue will also construct the other.

spaces.name: Windows
spaces.benefit: Building one stained glass window will automatically build the other hotspots in the Chapel.

spaces.name: Rug
spaces.benefit: If the furniture is removed, player will receive their Raging echoes rug back, allowing them to move it to a different room or sell it to another player.

spaces.name: Centrepiece
spaces.benefit: A focal centrepiece is required for the house owner to direct the portals. The higher level greater teleport focus is for cosmetic purpose only, meaning just a teleport focus will suffice for creat…

spaces.name: Portals
spaces.benefit: The higher tier versions are just cosmetic upgrades.

spaces.name: Big plant / Small plant
spaces.benefit: Note: As with all plantable items in Construction, the player will receive the same amount of experience for Construction and Farming.

spaces.name: Big plant 2 / Small plant 2
spaces.benefit: Note: As with all plantable items in Construction, the player will receive the same amount of experience for Construction and Farming.

spaces.name: Centrepiece
spaces.benefit: It is mainly for decoration, though it can be used as a water source.

spaces.name: Hedging
spaces.benefit: Note: As with all plantable items in Construction, the player will receive the same amount of experience for Construction and Farming.

spaces.name: Tip jar
spaces.benefit: Guests in a player's house may use the tip jar to gift coins and platinum tokens to the house owner.

spaces.name: Decoration
spaces.benefit: Decorations are hung on walls, and are purely for aesthetic purposes. The 'shield' class of decorations will reflect the family crest told to the player by Sir Renitee, the Falador Herald.

spaces.name: Floor
spaces.benefit: There are several different types of traps in this room. The steel cage trap can only trap your opponents in the cage; a trapdoor can drop opponents into an oubliette, if there is one below the thr…

spaces.name: Lever
spaces.benefit: The lever, if pulled, can trigger the centre trap that is in this throne room. It can also be used by the house owner to set challenge mode and activate the house Dungeon monsters and traps, and to…

spaces.name: Seating
spaces.benefit: These are only used for sitting and watching. The two bench hotspots here are the same as in the dining room, so the same flatpacks can be used.

spaces.name: Throne
spaces.benefit: Building any of these thrones will make both thrones appear in both spots.

spaces.name: Trapdoor
spaces.benefit: The trapdoor gives access to the oubliette, if there is one below the throne room. Only the house owner may use this.

spaces.name: Fence
spaces.benefit: For players purchasing all supplies from TzHaar-Hur-Tel or TzHaar-Hur-Zal, the total cost will range 593,127-594,627 Tokkul with Karamja gloves, or 684,377-685,877 Tokkul without.

spaces.name: Pool
spaces.benefit: The pool space will restore certain stats, depending on the type of pool built. Note: You can use the crystal saw for an invisible +3 boost, combined with either tea for a visible up to +3 boost (t…

spaces.name: Teleport
spaces.benefit: The teleport space allows players to plant a fairy ring (code ), spirit tree, or obelisk, allowing quick transportation, provided they have completed the quests required to use them.

spaces.name: Theme
spaces.benefit: The sulphur vent, like those found in Mor Ul Rek, acts as a fire, allowing players to cook raw fish/meat, but not food that requires a cooking range, such as uncooked pies.

spaces.name: Topiary
spaces.benefit: Players can have the topiaries sculpted into various boss heads with a pair of secateurs or magic secateurs, provided they have killed the boss at least once.

spaces.name: Seating (2 hotspots)
spaces.benefit: Unlike the teak garden bench and gnome bench, this bench cannot be sat on due to rendering issues.

spaces.name: Amulet
spaces.benefit: There are two separate slots to mount amulets from, one for each that can be mounted. Only one of each amulet can be mounted.

spaces.name: Curtains
spaces.benefit: If another room is placed behind a pair of curtain hotspots such that it blocks the windows, the windows and curtains will be replaced with a wall decoration depending on the type of curtains.

spaces.name: Rug
spaces.benefit: If the furniture is removed, player will receive their Raging echoes rug back, allowing them to move it to a different room or sell it to another player.

spaces.name: Portal Nexus
spaces.benefit: The portal nexus can also be used to scry similar to a scrying pool.

spaces.name: Altar
spaces.benefit: The altar hot spot allows players to build a spellbook-switching altar. They can be used to switch spellbooks without having to travel to the overworld spellbook-switching altars or have the Magic…

spaces.name: Boss lair
spaces.benefit: The boss lair allows a player to build a fancy display showing off various bosses. In order to display a boss lair, players must have killed the boss once, and use the jar dropped by that boss on t…

spaces.name: Display
spaces.benefit: The mounted display displays certain items to show off the player's items or wealth.

spaces.name: Jewellery box
spaces.benefit: The jewellery box can store various teleportation jewellery. Each box will provide unlimited teleports to locations provided by the enchanted jewellery.

spaces.name: Quest list
spaces.benefit: The quest list displays the player's progress through every quest and miniquest. It will show which quests the player has completed, started and not started.

spaces.name: Decoration
spaces.benefit: Making this fills both of the decoration spaces in the room.

spaces.name: Floor
spaces.benefit: The centre floor is where players fall into from a throne room. If the player has already built a cage with a trap inside, both the cage and the contents inside must be removed to upgrade the trap.

spaces.name: Guard
spaces.benefit: Guards are activated when challenge mode is turned on and will attack nearby players. A spicy stew or a Construction tea can be used to boost to the required level.

spaces.name: Ladder
spaces.benefit: If challenge mode is enabled, only the house owner can use this ladder. Warning: Make sure to not instant click as the room can be removed completely!

spaces.name: Prison
spaces.benefit: Players have to pick the lock (using Thieving), or force the lock (using Strength) of the gate, to get out.

spaces.name: Decoration
spaces.benefit: Making this fills both of the decoration spaces in the room.

spaces.name: Door
spaces.benefit: Players have to pick the lock (using Thieving) or force the lock (using Strength) to open dungeon doors.

spaces.name: Guard
spaces.benefit: Guards are activated when challenge mode is turned on and will attack nearby players. A spicy stew or a Construction tea can be used to boost to the required level.

spaces.name: Rug/Stairs
spaces.benefit: Stairs can be used to connect to a skill hall, quest hall, or a dungeon entrance in a garden or formal garden above.

spaces.name: Trap
spaces.benefit: Used as obstacles. There is a chance that when a player steps on a trap, it will not activate.

spaces.name: Decoration
spaces.benefit: Making this fills both of the decoration spaces in the room.

spaces.name: Door
spaces.benefit: Players have to pick the lock (using Thieving) or force the lock (using Strength) to open dungeon doors.

spaces.name: Monster
spaces.benefit: The guardian monster has to be killed before a player can get the treasure.

spaces.name: Treasure
spaces.benefit: The treasure can only be opened once the guardian has been killed, with the maximum amount of coins that can be stored dependent on the type of chest built.
